name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+22 district fundamentals favor Democrats even with the seat open
Gilbert holds a roughly five-to-one fundraising advantage over Brown
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent
$2.3 million in outside spending against Gilbert is the one sign of a contest
model.rationale: A D+22 open seat still leans heavily Democratic, and Gilbert's decisive fundraising edge over Brown reinforces the structural advantage. Outside groups have spent heavily against Gilbert, but with no polls or expert ratings showing a competitive race and markets pricing Democrats near certain, the seat stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: Fresh polling or sustained opposition spending showing Gilbert well below the district's typical Democratic margin would justify softening toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Florida's 24th District, based in Miami-Dade and Broward counties, carries a partisan lean of about 22 points toward Democrats. Frederica Wilson's retirement created an open seat, but the district's fundamentals still strongly favor the Democratic nominee, Oliver Gilbert. Gilbert has raised roughly $1.5 million, far outpacing Republican Te Mayonna Brown's $313,000, and prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 95 percent.

The main wrinkle is outside spending: groups have put about $2.3 million into opposing Gilbert, an unusually large sum for a district this blue. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and market pricing. Nothing in the evidence suggests a Republican win is realistic, keeping the seat in the Safe Democratic column.
